topic: Life Cycle of an Exhaustible Non-Renewable Resource (Hubbert Curve)
questionText:
Arrange the stages of non-renewable fossil fuel exploitation according to the Hubbert bell-shaped production curve:
(I) Initial discovery and early extraction: rapid exponential growth as easily accessible, shallow reserves are tapped
(II) Peak Production (Hubbert Peak): maximum extraction rate is reached when approximately half of all recoverable reserves are exhausted
(III) Post-Peak Deceleration: production begins irreversible terminal decline as remaining reserves become deeper and costlier to extract
(IV) Economic depletion / Abandonment: energy return on investment (EROI) collapses near 1:1, rendering remaining reserves economically unviable

Choose the correct chronological/logical sequence from the options given below:

options.text: I -> II -> III -> IV

options.text: IV -> II -> III -> I
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Hubbert curve progression: discovery boom, peak production, post-peak contraction, and economic exhaustion when EROI collapses.
Hence Option C is correct.
Hence, option (A) is correct.

questionText: The 'Half-Life' (t_1/2) of a radioactive isotope (e.g. Cesium-137 with t_1/2 = 30 years, or Plutonium-239 with t_1/2 = 24,100 years) is defined as the time required for:

options.text: Exactly half of the radioactive parent nuclei in a sample to undergo decay into daughter products
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Half-Life Concept in Radioactive Decay.

options.text: The complete elimination of 100% of all radioactivity from the universe
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: The atomic nucleus to double its physical weight
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: The temperature of the isotope to drop to absolute zero
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Half-Life Concept in Radioactive Decay (Environmental and Natural Resource Economics):
Half-life is the characteristic time required for 50% of radioactive atoms to disintegrate. Long-lived isotopes (Pu-239, t1/2 = 24,100 yrs) require geological isolation for millennia.
Hence Option C is correct.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.

questionText:
Match the radioisotope in List I with its signature property/half-life in List II:

List I:
(A) Iodine-131
(B) Cesium-137
(C) Carbon-14
(D) Plutonium-239

List II:
(I) Half-life of 8 days; concentrates in thyroid gland; used in medical radiotherapy
(II) Half-life of 30 years; major persistent gamma-emitting fission product contaminating soils
(III) Half-life of 5,730 years; cosmogenically formed isotope used for radiocarbon dating archaeological organic remains
(IV) Half-life of 24,100 years; fissile transuranic actinide used in nuclear weapons and breeder reactors

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

options.text: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
I-131 has 8-day half-life; Cs-137 has 30-year half-life; C-14 has 5,730-year half-life; and Pu-239 has 24,100-year half-life.
Hence Option A is correct.
Hence, option (D) is the correct match.

questionText: When a government designates a virgin forest tract as an inviolate National Park, the 'Opportunity Cost' of that conservation decision represents:

options.text: The cost of building high-voltage electric perimeter fences
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: The monetary salary paid to national park forest guards
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: The total tourist entry ticket revenue collected annually
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

options.text: The forgone economic benefits that could have been generated if the land had been converted into commercial open-cast mining, timber logging, or agricultural estates
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for Opportunity Cost in Forest Conservation.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Environmental and Natural Resource Economics (Opportunity Cost in Forest Conservation):
The forgone economic benefits that could have been generated if the land had been converted into commercial open-cast mining, timber logging, or agricultural estates

Detailed Context:
Opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative forgone: by choosing conservation, society sacrifices the commercial revenue from mining or logging.
Hence Option B is correct.

Therefore, option (D) is the correct answer.
